Class ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.procedural.ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine
public class ThermohalineStommelAMOCEngine extends Object
Thermohaline Ocean Circulation invalid input: '&' Stommel 2-Box AMOC Tipping Point Engine (Henry Stommel, 1961).

Models the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) driven by thermal and haline density gradients:

  • Equation of State for Seawater Density: $$\rho(T, S) = \rho_0 \left[ 1 - \alpha_T (T - T_0) + \beta_S (S - S_0) \right]$$ with thermal expansion $\alpha_T \approx 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ K}^{-1}$ and haline contraction $\beta_S \approx 7.5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ PSU}^{-1}$.
  • Stommel Non-Linear 2-Box Overturning Flow ($q_{\text{AMOC}}$ in Sverdrups, $1\text{ Sv} = 10^6\text{ m}^3/\text{s}$): $$q = C \cdot \left[ \alpha_T (T_{\text{equator}} - T_{\text{pole}}) - \beta_S (S_{\text{equator}} - S_{\text{pole}}) \right]$$
  • Abrupt Tipping Point (Bifurcation): If meltwater discharge (e.g. from Greenland / Laurentide) freshens polar surface waters ($\Delta S_{\text{pole}} invalid input: '<' -2.5\text{ PSU}$), the AMOC collapses ($q \to 0$ or reverses), triggering a catastrophic high-latitude cooling of $-5^\circ\text{C}$ to $-10^\circ\text{C}$ (Younger Dryas / Heinrich event analogue).

      Calculates Stommel 2-box overturning circulation flux (in Sv) and climatic shift.
      Parameters:
      tempEquatorC - Equator surface temperature (~28°C)
      tempPoleC - Polar North Atlantic surface temperature (~2°C)
      salinityEquatorPsu - Equator salinity (~36.5 PSU)
      salinityPolePsu - Polar salinity (~34.5 PSU baseline, dropping during Heinrich meltwater events)
